key_insight: On-policy distillation makes many small, coordinate-sparse parameter updates rather than large widespread changes. These updates are spread across layers and often concentrated in FFN-related weights, showing that dense teacher supervision does not imply dense model updates.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of understanding of how on-policy distillation changes model parameters, especially why a method that uses dense supervision and on-policy data still produces sparse and structured updates.
method: Analyze on-policy distillation updates across multiple language and vision-language model pairs.
Measure update sparsity and geometry to see how parameter changes are distributed across coordinates and layers.
Compare update patterns under different use cases to identify consistent structural behaviors.
impact: This helps practitioners understand where training signal is actually being applied during distillation, which can guide debugging, optimization, and parameter-efficient adaptation strategies. It also suggests that sparse-update behavior may be a useful property to exploit in future post-training methods.
visual_elements: Layer-wise heatmap of parameter update magnitudes showing sparse activation patterns
Diagram of student trajectories with dense teacher supervision in on-policy distillation
Bar chart comparing sparsity across layers or module types (attention vs FFN)
Vector field or geometry illustration showing update direction and concentration
paper_title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Guo Yu, Wenlin Liu, Yulan Hu, Hao-Xuan Ma, Jun-Peng Jiang
